reviews.text: Always courteous and helpful

I boarded my dog, Saffron, here starting Wednesday night, and she has had nonstop, severe diarrhea ever since coming home.

Saffron is boarded frequently at another trusted facility and has never once had gastrointestinal distress, stress colitis, or illness after a stay. While boarding facilities love to write off digestive issues as "routine separation anxiety," that excuse does not hold up for a dog who is well-socialized and completely accustomed to boarding environments.

This points directly to an issue with facility conditions—whether due to lapses in sanitation, cross-contamination between dogs, or unauthorized dietary changes/treats.

Dealing with the stress of a sick dog, days of clean-up, and veterinary bills to run fecal panels is completely unacceptable for a professional boarding operation.

I will not be returning, and I strongly caution other owners against leaving their dogs here.

On March 29, 2026, our beloved family dog, Buttercup, passed away. Buttercup was a beautiful white Golden Retriever who had been a cherished member of the Herron family for nearly eleven years.

She provided unconditional love, loyalty, companionship, and brought joy to everyone she met. Buttercup was loved not only by our family but also by many friends whose lives she touched throughout the years. She was more than a pet—she was family.

After her passing, my son searched online for a place that could help us through this difficult time. We found Hyde Park Animal Hospital on Stoney Island, right in our neighborhood. During one of the hardest moments our family has faced, their staff treated us with compassion, patience, and dignity.

The veterinary nurse respectfully assisted my son in removing Buttercup from the car and carefully placing her on a stretcher. Every step of the process was handled with kindness and professionalism, giving our family comfort and peace during our time of grief.

We chose to have our beloved Buttercup cremated, and we are grateful for the care and respect shown to her and our family. We will forever cherish the memories, love, and happiness she brought into our lives.

Run free, sweet Buttercup. You will always hold a special place in our hearts and will never be forgotten. All Dogs goes To Heaven.

My cat had been seen a few times by the staff at HPAH without incident. Apparently, during the last visit, the vet added a message in her medical notes that she required a sedative before the vet would see her for future visits. Which is contrary to the "good behavior" feedback we had received at past visits. And contrary to her groomer's positive behavior feedback--appointments which involve baths and nail trims.

We set up an appointment weeks in advance, and received multiple email reminders--none of which stated she "required" a sedative for the visit. On the day of the visit, I sprayed her carrier with a lavender calming spray--something I do for all pets prior to car travel. We arrived, and the receptionist asked if we had given her a sedative. I stated that we did not have any sedative and that I had used calming spray in her carrier. She then went into a room and came back a few minutes later and said the vet would not see our cat for her visit. She said it is in the medical notes that our cat needed to be sedated for her visits. I inquired as to why none of the reminders stated that she would not be seen if she was not sedated--and was told it was a vet requirement.

I told her we did not have the sedative, it was not clearly communicated that she "required" a sedative for a visit, and that we would be finding a new veterinary clinic. They emailed the medical notes to me--to prove the vet required it--a note at the very bottom of our kitty's medical notes recommending she be sedated for her future visit. The email response also included a snide note that "If I didn't know sedation was required, why would I have used calming spray?" As if to insinuate I substituted the sedation with a pet calming spray in an attempt to pull one over on a vet who was frightened of my kitty. To which I replied that calming spray was a standard practice for all pets in my household for any car travel.

After this experience, we decided that our cat will be cared for by another clinic/veterinarian in the future. I understand that client concerns can be downplayed on review sites as angry, emotional, etc. Reread the 1-2 star reviews and see if there are any themes regarding poor communication. You/the client can decide if you want to waste your time--take off work, put your pet through car travel--only to be told the vet won't see your pet when you arrive on time for your scheduled visit.

EDIT: I'm not sure what's worse: ignoring the reviews or responding 11 months later. The new vet has been amazing. Shockingly, no sedation needed.

Everyone is very nice but communication is atrocious and it impacts animal health. A year or two ago I brought my cat in to get tested for a uti. Didn’t get results, despite calling, and going in person, for two weeks. She had a uti the entire time and to this day i wonder if it impacted my cat’s recurring kidney problems. Have also had delays with prescriptions, including for serious issues like her UTI or for food refills. And several times a year I make an appointment that they then claim I got wrong (time, location, the appt existing).

Recently, I went in because my cat was vomiting often. The vet felt an unidentified mass in my cat’s abdomen. They couldn't do an xray because their machine was down so scheduled me for Monday. They brought her back from getting an anti-nausea shot and she was very upset, which she does usually get. They came back minutes later to say they'd "forgotten to draw blood." Decided to schedule that for Monday too.

Monday, we got xrays, bloodwork, and other tests done, all for the usual exorbitant prices. They warned me Dr Baker would be out for a week and that I wouldn’t get my results for 7 days and that she'd call Monday. They did not give me more meds for my cat in the meantime. That afternoon Dr Baker called and said the xray showed an irregularity with the kidney and asked if I wanted to send it to a radiologist for $200+ more.

I spent 7 full days watching over my cat, who remained sick, and stressing. On the day the doc returned I spent all day waiting for results. At 4:30 I called and they said I “might still get a call.” 5:30 they said she was gone for the day. I informed them I had not gotten one, and they seemed puzzled. The next day, no call, and I was told she went home early for a personal emergency and would be out til Friday.  They saw in the file that they were waiting on one test still but that I should have gotten a Monday followup call. Friday I called twice to emphasize that I needed to hear back, and finally got a call from her 10 minutes to the clinic closing. There was no mass. Possible IBS. Kidney was the same as it usually is. Heart was borderline but it would be fine because "she's never had a heart murmur." She does have a heart murmur, I corrected her. She's always had one, it's noted at every appointment. Oh yes, she said. I should have checked my notes.

Six calls in five days. 10 days of waiting to find out if my cat is ok, and worrying she has something that needs treatment. All that to have the doctor finally get in touch and she hasn't even looked down at my cat's file properly. I have made an appointment for another vet. I will never bring my cat back there. Other reviews mention that Dr Williams is excellent; but I've only ever seen Dr Baker, and the reviews are not good for her. Skip this practice and go elsewhere unless you don't have a choice.

I have been taking my dogs here because I live in the area.  I’d imagine this place stays in business due to its convenient location and lack of competitors in the area.  It most definitely is not their professionalism that is bringing in clients.  If there was any somewhat convenient alternative in the neighborhood, I’d be there in a heartbeat.

I had a generally good experience with this clinic in the past (the vet techs are so nice and great), but felt really let down in a recent critical situation. When I first brought in my two young sibling cats, I asked if it would be possible to do an early spay/neuter, knowing the risks of them mating. I was told they don’t fix cats until 6 months unless necessary. When my female 5 month old kitten went into heat for the first time and was mated by her intact male sibling, they refused a spay, even though pregnancy at her young age is more dangerous than a spay in early heat. I was also told they don’t do pregnancy terminations, and that the only option was to separate them for 6-8 weeks until they’d be willing to do a spay, which does nothing to eliminate the risk of pregnancy if mating has already occurred. They offered no other solutions and were completely unwilling to be flexible on their policies despite the potential health risks for my pets, and their website advertising flexibility in special/emergency situations. The price was also incredibly steep— over 4x the cost of what I ended up paying at a different clinic (who also emphasized that early fixing was the more responsible choice at this stage). I left feeling like my concerns weren’t taken seriously and wasn’t offered real support to protect my cats’ health. In fact, I believe they prioritized their own “image” and policies as a clinic rather than their patients’ wellness. This may be the right vet for some people, but if you have intact cats or urgent reproductive concerns, you may want to ask detailed questions first. I will be taking my cats elsewhere moving forward to a place that is more willing to prioritize their patients’ needs and safety.

The vet Kat had a bad attitude, not relatable. She was acting as if it was an issue to ask her questions. I’m spending almost $500 on service and it was an issue to ask her questions. Will not go back.

I took my dog here for years before finally taking her somewhere else and I’m so thankful I finally did. Overpriced, they charge you for services you didn’t receive, hide fees until after, don’t answer the phones, take weeks for medication refills, and never return calls. There are better options!

Never bringing my cats here again. I brought both of my cats to be seen due to excessive scratching and hair loss around their ears. The first veterinarian they saw prescribed them itch wipes. When I brought them back for a follow-up they scheduled me with a different veterinarian (unbeknownst to me ) who sent us home with a clean bill of health after seeing the improvements in my cat's skin. When we got home, my cats immediately started scratching again to the point of bleeding. I had already expressed my concerns at the veterinarian because I felt like her follow-up was not thorough enough but I was dismissed. When I called the vet back and explained what had happened less than 30 minutes since they had been seen, They told me I had to reschedule another appointment with the first veterinarian and pay full price. At this point, I had already given them over $400, money that I did not have being that I was unemployed at the time. Because I did not have any more funds for them to be seen again after the vets negligence, my cats have been wearing cones and scratching for the past 7 months whole I've been trying to find at home remedies.  I'm just now able to save up enough to take them to a new veterinarian. Thank you for all your amazing help Hyde Park animal hospital!!!!

I’d like to send a special thank you the staff and vets at this location. Both my dogs Sir Ellington and Paris were patients here. This year we unfortunately lost them both. Sir Ellington suffered from Congestive Heart Failure and collapsed trachea. Both progressive conditions I believe common in Yorkies. The care he was provided sustained him throughout the remaining years we had with him even as we changed vets due to relocation and I just want to thank you for taking the time, completing the test, and making needed modifications to his regimen that truly got it right. Although we were cross county I was actually planning on bringing him back during his last rough patch because I wanted him to be seen by the team who were most successful at his protocol but he didn’t make it. It took me a while to write this and I can’t fight back the tears. They both were so loved and will be dearly missed but I hope you all continue the great work you are doing because they are not pets. They are family. Thank you team.

This place is a disaster! I seriously believe that I was scammed. Felt like I was being punked and I was. All these vaccinations are required for you to have your dog groomed or boarded. Ok. So I met with the Vet for an exam. Then I had to come back to get more vaccinations. Then I had to come back in 3 weeks for more. Hundreds of dollars spent. They also tried to tell me that he needed a rabies vaccine. No he didn’t. That doesn’t expire until next year. After all “required” vaccines were completed I was finally able to schedule an appointment to have him groomed. I dropped him off. They call me 10 mins later to tell me that they weren’t able to groom him because one of the test results required more time to process. Then why take my money, schedule the grooming and waste my time having me drop him off? So I had to leave work and go back to pick him up. I called to let them know that I was on my way back. No answer so I left a voicemail. I get there again and they tell me they can now groom him because he already had that test at a previous vet that had not expired. Are you kidding me? So why waste my money on this test again? And why didn’t you call me to tell me that he can now be groomed. So now I’m headed back to work. They call me again and tell me that he can not be groomed. He’s too old. So we’ll have to shave him completely bald and charge you more money. Come back for the 3rd time today and get your dog. They did nothing but waste my time and money. I will take the long commute to the vet that is more professional and organized. This place is a mess and can’t be trusted.

Our 7 year old pit-mix male dog KennyBlu saw Dr. Jeremy Williams and his team. They were awesome. Kenny is a sweet dog and they treated him with gentle care and no fear because of his breed. Everyone from the receptionist to the tech the doctor and dr's. assistant were professional and answered all of our questions. At one point we had 3 techs assisting, administering vaccines and teaching who seemed to be a student assistant the proper way to administer and draw blood. Dr. Jeremy called me a few days later with KennyBlu's lab results and review of the exams. He was very attentive and explained everything in laymen's terms so I could get full understanding. The office was clean and didn't smell as so many animal hospitals do. We plan to bring Kenny back for his healthcare and follow up visits.

I have been using this place since they were a clinic on 53rd Street and I continue to use the clinic on 51st now, with the hospital as a medication refill spot. I have never had issues with anyone, until now, and I do not even know who caused this problem!

I called and left a refill request for my dog's medication on their phone service on Monday. Nothing. No acknowledgment at all. I called and left a message Wednesday asking for an update, because of course no one ever picks up the phone. Nothing. Called yesterday and left a message again. Nothing. Called this morning, AGAIN, and left a message saying that I had left a refill request, my dog was down to his last pill, and I really didn't want him to get sick (he has allergies that make him wheeze). No response. FINALLY, I received a phone call saying that his prescription needed to be approved by his vet, but since he wasn't there until next Wednesday, they were going to ask another vet to approve it, but they may not because this vet has never seen my dog before. WHAT?! She apologized because someone obviously dropped the ball, but I guess there isn't much that she can do.

Now I have to figure out what to do for my dog until if and when his prescription is refilled. Frankly, I'm tired of the runaround I got with this request and will probably just be looking for another place that will hopefully be more timely with their refills and calls.

I’m extremely disappointed and frustrated with the service I received at Hyde Park Animal Hospital today. I had a confirmed appointment — they even sent me an email confirmation — so I left work early to make sure my dog could be seen. When I arrived, I was told there was a scheduling error on their end and the doctor would not be seeing my pet.

What’s most upsetting is the complete lack of professionalism and compassion. The doctor didn’t even come out to speak to me personally, didn’t offer an apology, and made zero effort to assess whether my dog had an urgent need. Instead, the message was simply relayed through the front desk that the doctor “couldn’t see us.”

This is unacceptable for any medical practice — especially one entrusted with the care of animals. My time was wasted, my dog wasn’t treated, and I was left with no support, no solution, and no basic courtesy. I will not be returning and cannot recommend this clinic to anyone who values reliability, communication, and basic decency in pet care.

0 stars. TERRIBLE business operations and SHAMEFUL tactics. VERY UNPROFESSIONAL SCAMMERS. They will book an appointment over the phone, quote you a price and then play nice once you're in just to do the old switch-a-roo when you're already done with part of the "services".

Brought my two 10 week old puppies in for their first set of shots. We were told over the phone that the cost would be $60 per dog for their first round. Never told there was a exam fee that cost more than the actual shots and dewormer.

Upon arrival a lady snatched both puppies out of my two daughters hands without our permission while I was turned around singing in and she ran off with them to another room to "show them off".

The doctor came in with no gloves on and touched around them and in their mouths with his bare hands for less than 5 full mins. for both puppies just to tell us after the fact that it was $75+ per pup per exam. He barely did anything at all. BFFR.

They were upset and shocked when I said I wanted all services performed in front of us as I know the type of games people play nowadays.  They were moving weird which alarmed my instincts to keep a close watch and to make sure the service claimed would actually be provided/performed; not off in another room where we wouldn't see them as the vet suggested or tried to run game on me.

They charged two different prices for both pups of the same age and breed that had a clean bill of health from them. Wanted over $450 for just one round of exams and shots for both which is outrageous pricing and was not discussed over the phone. There's no pricing sheet like other vets in the Chicagoland area so they can make up whatever as they go after they already have you in there.

Petco charges way less for all the round of shots which is done in 3 visits plus extra services and testing. At Hyde Park animal hospital she told me after the fact that going forward every time they come there is an exam fee plus the cost of shots; so if I agreed to the insanity I would be over paying for subpar services that I'm not sure would have even been performed.

$450+ x 4 visits totaling over $1800. Petco charges $229 for Pup Shield Pro (all 3 visits) or $99 per pup first visit and the exams for new patients are free.

Save yourself time, money and the headache of dealing with people that like to play mind games and go with a well know company that lays everything out so there's no confusion. Do yourself a favor and DO NOT go here just because it's close by. The fake niceness is a rouse unless you just like overpaying then do you.

AND always always always read the reviews and don't ignore the people that take the time to warn you. I should have read the reviews they are horrible.

Next appointment wasn't until April 30, and when I called back they did not answer the phone. Its not only inconsiderate to cancel us same day but to also be unapologetic about it is despicable. Thankfully, Woodlawn Animal Hospital was able to take us same day, so we will not be returning to Hyde Park.

They Killed my puppy, and broke our heart. She was my daughters Emotional Support Animal. My grief is so heavy it cuts off my breath. I am angry I trusted Hyde Park Animal Hospital.
The many choices they made lead to the death of my puppy. 1) not informing me of medicine used on her when she arrived.  2) not letting us know the critical nature of her condition 3)not releasing her early enough to get to ER.

She only lived 1 hr in the ER, and we were at Hyde Pk hospital for approximately 5 hrs. When they determined they did not have the capability to treat her- they should have released us to rush her to ER.  Instead they suggested that we leave her with them overnight for "observation." Then take her to ER the next day if no improvement. They close at 7pm, and open 8am. There would be NO ONE ON SITE @ NIGHT. My baby would have died alone.  That suggestion implied that her condition was not critical.  If it was critical then I would've trust that they wouldn't suggest leaving her there for "observation." When we brought her in - she had thrown up & we were concerned. Roxy had an ear infection diagnosis a week before. We just wanted her checked out. We came in - She was up moving around on the exam table- in my lap- my shoulder--the only issue was she was not feeling well. I didn't think I would be burying her hours later.

The problem is they KNEW SHE WAS CRITICAL.   Her records were transferred to ER.  Literally when we entered the ER specialist runs out grab my puppy and says to her team "this is our critical patient". This was the FIRST TIME I HEARD CRITICAL, and the LAST TIME I SAW MY BABY ALIVE.

Why didnt they tell me, and give me a chance to leave to rush her to ER quicker? Major part of this horrible grief I feel is that I trusted, and waited to take her to Hyde Park Hosp. My puppy was up & alert when I brought her in after she threw up, etc. They gave her to me in a blanket barely coherent as i rushed her to ER. I am angry at myself. Instead I should have bypassed them, and go to ER. Now my 2 yr old puppy is dead, and my heart is broken. I can't stop crying, and being angry at Hyde Park  AND Myself.

The trust I had for them died with my fur baby. I can no longer pick her up, cradle her, rub her, and gaze into her soothing puppy dog eyes. I now hold my hands upon my heart imagining her resting her head on my shoulder. That was a heavy price to pay for the lesson. This has been devastating for our family-she was not only my "grand-puppy" - she saved my daughter. Now my daughters Emotional Support Animal is gone. 😢.  This is a nightmare I wish I could wake up from.  Pray for our family... 🙏
